entry.evidence: 2026-08-02: a 40-minute checkout outage read as p99 latency drift because the payment client retried forever; the upstream had been returning 502 since minute one.
entry.falsifier: an unbounded retry loop where operators still identified the dependency failure as fast as a bounded one would have shown it.
entry.lesson: A retry loop with exponential backoff and no attempt ceiling will keep a caller alive indefinitely against a dependency that is simply gone. The symptom presented to operators is latency, not failure, so the real outage is discovered hours late. Cap total attempts, then surface the last error verbatim rather than swallowing it.

entry.evidence: 2026-08-05: the render worker restarted 3,400 times over two days on a malformed asset; dashboards were green throughout.
entry.falsifier: a supervisor with no restart ceiling whose operators still noticed a permanent fault as quickly as a bounded one would have surfaced it.
entry.lesson: Automatic restart of a wedged worker is a repair when the wedge is transient and a disguise when it is not. With no restart ceiling the process group stays nominally healthy while the same defect fires every few seconds, and nothing in the health signal distinguishes the two cases. Bound the restarts and escalate on exhaustion, so a permanent fault becomes visible instead of absorbed.

entry.evidence: 2026-07-20: the warning count had grown to 1,900 over a year and no single warning was ever actioned until they became blocking.
entry.falsifier: a codebase that sustained a non-zero warning count for a year and still actioned regressions promptly.
entry.lesson: Warnings that do not block are warnings nobody fixes. Promote every lint warning to a build failure: the backlog is paid down once, and after that the signal stays at zero where a regression is obvious.

entry.evidence: 2026-07-28: after lint became blocking, --no-verify usage rose sharply and two genuine test failures were pushed through the same escape hatch.
entry.falsifier: a team with blocking lint whose bypass-flag usage did not rise.
entry.lesson: A build that fails on cosmetics teaches the team that the gate is noise, and the habit they learn is bypassing it -- including on the day it catches something real. Keep lint advisory and reserve build failure for correctness.

entry.evidence: 2026-08-06: a 12-second dependency blip produced three sharp retry spikes at 1s, 2s and 4s before jitter was added.
entry.falsifier: a fleet retrying on undithered exponential backoff that does not show synchronized retry spikes after a common failure instant.
entry.lesson: Exponential backoff alone makes every client that failed at the same instant retry at the same instant. Add full jitter to the delay so the retry wave spreads instead of arriving as a second thundering herd.

entry.evidence: 2026-08-07: with a 5s cap against a 30s upstream timeout, one logical request became six concurrent in-flight calls.
entry.falsifier: a backoff ceiling below the callee timeout that does not produce overlapping in-flight attempts.
entry.lesson: If the maximum backoff delay is shorter than the callee's own request timeout, a retry is issued while the previous attempt is still running, and load multiplies exactly when the dependency is weakest. Set the ceiling above the callee timeout.
